If we desire a statement with a different confidence level, the value of $t$ must be changed. For example, at 99\% confidence the corresponding $t$ value is approximately 2.680, leading to bounds of

\begin{equation*}
3,014.16 \pm 2.680 \cdot \frac{1,537.55}{\sqrt{50}} = 3,014.16 \pm 582.74
\end{equation*}
and the interval estimate is [2,431.42,\hspace{0.5em} 3,596.90]. This creates a 99\% two-sided confidence interval for the total monthly salary cost in a population of 2,222 employees: [5,402,625, 7,992,302]. Note that the 99\% confidence interval is wider than the 95\% confidence interval.
